Enterprise AI decisions, explained

How do we assess whether our organisation is ready for enterprise AI?

Start with the business decision or workflow, then assess data quality and access, integration dependencies, cloud controls, skills and accountable ownership. Readiness is specific to a use case: identify gaps and evidence needed before expanding investment.

How do we decide which AI use cases justify investment?

Compare expected business value with delivery cost, ongoing inference and support costs, adoption effort and risk. Establish a baseline and measurable success criteria. Prioritise opportunities where the evidence supports AI over simpler alternatives.

How do we design secure and scalable AI architecture?

Define trust boundaries and enforce least-privilege access in the application and tools. Design data flows, retrieval, approval steps, capacity limits, monitoring and recovery together. Test misuse and dependency failures before increasing exposure.

Should we use AWS or Azure for enterprise AI?

Evaluate the existing enterprise cloud estate, identity and data platforms, workload needs, model options, regional availability and operating costs. Amazon Bedrock and Microsoft Foundry are options to assess against those constraints; neither is the right default for every organisation.

What is required to move an AI prototype into production?

Beyond model quality, establish evaluation criteria, secure integration, data governance, deployment controls, observability, capacity and cost limits, recovery procedures and a support owner. Expand through controlled releases with explicit acceptance criteria.

What should an enterprise AI transformation roadmap include?

Include prioritised use cases, architecture decisions, readiness gaps, dependencies, accountable owners, phased investment assumptions and success measures. Define review gates so later commitments depend on evidence from earlier work.
